newsitem.title: CANADA: Pipeline outage cuts half Canada's oil movement.
newsitem.headline: Pipeline outage cuts half Canada's oil movement.

text.p: A massive weekend outage on the pipeline system that moves most of Canada's crude oil exports to the United States forced half of the country's total oil supply to a halt, wreaking havoc among producers and refiners, industry officials said on Monday.

Interprovincial Pipe Line Co., the world's longest crude oil pipeline system, was forced to shut down most of its operation after a power failure in storm-battered Minnesota knocked out three pumping stations in the state late Saturday.

Edmonton, Alberta-based Interprovincial said one million barrels a day of crude oil -- about half of Canada's total production -- stopped moving to key U.S. and eastern Canadian refining markets. The pumping stations, powered by Minnesota-based Otter Tail Power Co., were not expected to be fixed until at least Wednesday.
The pipeline system was moving about 1.4 million barrels a day at the time of the shutdown.
"It's very unusal -- the severity of the storm and the amount of impact it has had," Interprovincial spokesman Alan Roth said.
The Interprovincial system consists of a series of adjacent lines that extend 1,098 miles (1,767 kms) to Superior, Wisconsin from Edmonton via Saskatchewan, Manitoba and Minnesota.

At Superior, where Interprovincial has a huge tank farm for storage, its affiliated Lakehead Pipe Line moves the oil to the U.S. Midwest -- which comprises about 15 percent of U.S. refining capacity -- and southern Ontario, Canada's industrial heartland.

The pumping stations were affected by the same electricity disruption that left 62 towns in Minnesota and North Dakota without power on Monday after the region was slammed by a severe weekend ice-, snow- and windstorm.

The Minnesota disruptions forced the pipeline to shut its lines down between Edmonton and Superior -- a move that could cause oil to build up to the capacity of storage in western Canada and force companies to stop oil wells from pumping.

Crude oil traders in Canada estimated that the Chicago refining market was short 250,000 barrels per day light grade crude and 400,000 barrels per day of gooey heavy oil, Canada's fastest-growing grade of oil supply.

In southern Ontario, refineries were receiving oil from storage at Wisconsin, but the pipeline that flows to Sarnia, Ontario from Superior was also expected to shut down early Tuesday, Interprovincial said.
Interprovincial is a wholly owned unit of Calgary-based IPL Energy Inc.
